originality.rationale: A specific, exactly sharp fourth raw sampling-moment boundary and general cone-order monotonicity for zero-order-hold double-integrator feedback are not stated in the most relevant inspected primary literature; general stochastic-stability criteria and covariance-lifting methods are acknowledged as prior art. residual_risks: The full text of Agniel–Jury (1971), DOI 10.1137/0309027, remained inaccessible after ordinary open-access attempts; institutional route returned a connectivity limitation. Early randomly sampled control literature may contain a specialized implication.
The 2004 Montestruque–Antsaklis article was only partially material-inspected; coverage of all appendices or indirect specializations has not been excluded.
A failed semantic database search is not evidence of uniqueness; the first-three-moment premise and zero-order-hold normalization are important to the novelty comparison.

value.rationale: First three sampling moments alone fail to determine feedback mean-square stability even on fixed strictly positive support. The exact kurtosis-sensitive threshold is distribution independent over a natural prescribed-statistics class, and fourth-moment monotonicity provides a structural robust stability law rather than a one-off computed eigenvalue.
